minutes.headline: Board adopted a reappointment form (due Aug 15) and held over town manager appointments; Summer Street funded for 2017.
minutes.summary: The board heard that the Summer Street project was programmed on the 2017 regional transportation plan, and that design money may need a Chapter 90 commitment. It received the final report of the school committee's acceptance and diversity advisory committee. It voted to use a reappointment form for expiring terms and put off ratifying the town manager's appointments for a week. It also discussed manager goals, stormwater and committee reports.

votes.motion: Adopt the reappointment form for persons seeking reappointment for terms ending June 30, with forms due back by August 15.
Appoint Ken chenis as representative to the Joint Transportation committee.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member said the town must come up with the remaining local design funding, possibly from extra road money added to the budget. Chapter 90 money may have to be committed to keep the project moving.
The advisory committee gave a ballpark budget for programming, speakers, grant writer and training, ideally covered by grants and donations.
Payroll and accounts payable were read out, including the regional retirement payment due July 1 and several FY14 payables.
A member said complying with the first permit was costly and the new permit may bring more financial burden.

decisions.decision: Ratification of the town manager's appointment list put over to next week's agenda, with the field driver, technical advisory committee and inspector of animals to be clarified.
Board agreed to interview applicants and fill vacancies in July, starting with Council on Aging, Personnel committee and PACC, and take up reappointments in August.
Town manager and board goals put over to next week.

what_happened.line: The Select Board adopted a reappointment form for expiring terms, with completed forms due back by August 15.
Ratifying the town manager's appointment list was put over to next week, with several positions to be clarified first.
The board heard that the Summer Street project is programmed on the 2017 regional transportation plan and that local design money is still needed.
The board agreed to fill vacancies in July, starting with Council on Aging, Personnel and PACC, and to take up reappointments in August.
Town manager and board goals were put over to next week.

why_it_matters: Summer Street design work may draw on road money in the town budget, mostly taxes, or on Chapter 90 state road aid, which could leave less for other road repairs.
Residents interested in serving on town boards have a defined window: vacancies are filled in July and reappointments are handled in August.
watch_next: Next week's Select Board agenda: ratification of the town manager's appointments and the town manager and board goals.
